title: Collections Policy for Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements: Payments, Late Fees and Suspension
content:
**Policy.** Agreement charges are due the tier's payment terms days after they post and are paid by ACH, check or wire, or by card on tiers that accept cards, a credit card payment carrying the tier's surcharge percentage, rounded to the cent, half up. A late fee may post only after the grace period following the charge's due date has fully passed. The due date is the charge's posting date plus the tier's payment terms days, the grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after that due date, and the first late fee may post on the day after the grace period's last day. The late fee is the tier's monthly percentage of the past-due agreement balance with the tier's minimum as a floor, at most once per calendar month fee period. An agreement with a charge past due longer than the tier's suspension days is suspended, its entitlements, including any service call fee waiver, do not apply while suspended, and it is reinstated with the tier's reinstatement fee once the past-due balance is paid. A credit balance is refunded to the original tender within the refund processing business days.

This policy governs the payment of charges under the Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements.

## The agreement balance

The agreement balance is the amount the customer owes on the agreement. Fees and refunds raise it; payments, SLA credits, rebates and proration credits lower it.

## Due date and tender

- A charge is due on its posting date plus the tier's payment terms days.
- Charges are paid by ACH, check or wire, or by card on tiers that accept cards.
- A credit card payment carries the tier's surcharge percentage of that payment, rounded to the cent, half up, booked as one surcharge for that card payment.

*Hypothetical surcharge:* at an illustrative surcharge of 2.5 percent, a card payment of 641.30 carries 16.0325, rounded half up to 16.03.

## When a late fee may post

A late fee may post only after the grace period following the charge's due date has fully passed:

1. the due date is the posting date plus the tier's payment terms days;
2. the grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, for the tier's grace days;
3. the first late fee may post on the day after the grace period's last day.

*Date illustration (hypothetical dates and terms):* a charge posted on 1 March with 30 payment terms days is due on 31 March; a 10-day grace period runs from 1 April to 10 April; no late fee may post on or before 10 April, and the first late fee may post on 11 April.

## How much a late fee is

The late fee is the tier's monthly percentage of the past-due agreement balance, with the tier's minimum as a floor, and it posts at most once per calendar month fee period.

*Hypothetical figures (illustrative 1.2 percent and 20.00 minimum):* on a past-due balance of 900.00 the percentage gives 10.80, below the floor, so the fee is 20.00; on a past-due balance of 2,500.00 the percentage gives 30.00, above the floor, so the fee is 30.00. A second late fee in the same calendar month does not post.

## Suspension and reinstatement

- An agreement with a charge past due longer than the tier's suspension days is suspended, moving from active to suspended status. A charge past due for exactly the tier's suspension days is not yet past due longer than them.
- While suspended, the agreement's entitlements, including any service call fee waiver, do not apply.
- Once the past-due balance is paid, the agreement is reinstated to active status with the tier's reinstatement fee; the term start is unchanged by reinstatement.

## Refunds

A credit balance is refunded to the original tender within the refund processing business days, counted Monday to Friday excluding company holidays.
